event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: META’s 2022-02-03 filing frames COVID-19 as an ongoing, material, and multi-faceted enterprise risk.  Because the pandemic began less than two years before the filing date, the Time Decay Principle permits high scores when evidence shows concrete impact.  The company discloses both realised damage (e.g., the slowest advertising-revenue growth since IPO, supply-chain and labour shortages, price declines) and forward-looking uncertainty (volatile user behaviour, future ad-demand weakness, inability to predict duration, exposure to further lockdown measures).  Language is largely specific—citing a 10 % YoY ad-revenue figure, explicit references to reduced demand/pricing, infrastructure strain, and significant adverse impacts—rather than generic boiler-plate.  Several passages also connect the pandemic to second-order effects such as supply-chain disruption, logistics bottlenecks, labour shortages, and incremental infrastructure cost, directly matching the analysis focus.  Although some disclosures note temporary upside (spikes in user engagement), they are framed as transient and receding, thus heightening risk volatility.  Taken together, the filing presents a direct, recent, and quantitatively supported risk profile, meriting generally high snippet scores in the 5-9 range, moderated where impacts are less quantified or partly mitigated.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has previously had, and may in the future have, a significant adverse impact on our advertising revenue and also exposes our business to other risks.

components.reason: Explicitly states a significant adverse impact already experienced.
Highlights continuing, forward-looking exposure (“may in the future have”).
Links impact to core revenue stream (advertising).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, material, and ongoing threat to primary revenue yields a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, in the second quarter of 2020, our advertising revenue grew 10% year-over-year, which was the slowest growth rate for any fiscal quarter since our initial public offering.

components.reason: Quantifies impact with precise metric (10 % YoY, slowest since IPO).
Explicitly ties metric to pandemic context (“For example”).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Rare numeric disclosure of pandemic drag on revenue warrants strong score.

evidence_list.snippet: The effects of the pandemic previously resulted in reduced demand for our ads, a related decline in pricing of our ads, and additional demands on our technical infrastructure as a result of increased usage of our services, and any similar occurrences in the future may impair our ability to maintain or increase the quantity or quality of ads shown to users and adversely affect our revenue and financial results.

components.reason: Details three concrete impacts: demand drop, price decline, infrastructure strain.
Warns of future impairment to revenue and financial results.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Multi-dimensional, forward-looking damage across demand, pricing and capacity justifies high risk rating.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures have caused, and are continuing to cause, business slowdowns or shutdowns in certain affected countries and regions, which have previously significantly impacted our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Confirms ongoing operational disruption ('continuing to cause').
States prior significant impact on overall business and results.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct acknowledgement of sustained, significant global disruption yields solid score.

evidence_list.snippet: More recently, we believe this growth has moderated in many regions, and we may experience reduced advertising demand and related declines in pricing in future periods to the extent this trend continues, which could adversely affect our advertising revenue growth.

components.reason: Identifies reversal of earlier positive trend, signalling risk resurgence.
Links to future declines in demand, pricing, and revenue growth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking risk without hard numbers moderates but sustains concern.

evidence_list.snippet: Due to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, we have experienced, and expect to continue to experience, supply and labor shortages and other disruptions in logistics and the supply chain for our technical infrastructure.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to concrete supply-chain and labour shortages.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct tie to supply-chain—a focus area—earns mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: We have in the past experienced, and may in the future experience, volatility in our user and revenue growth rates as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, although we are unable to predict the duration or degree of such volatility with any certainty.

components.reason: States both realised and potential volatility in key metrics.
Highlights uncertainty ('unable to predict'), an aggravating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises unpredictability and metric volatility; lack of quantification tempers score.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, beginning in the first quarter of 2020, we experienced significant increases in the size and engagement of our active user base across a number of regions as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Shows pandemic-driven usage spike, indicating operating volatility.
‘Significant’ but beneficial impact acts as partial mitigation to revenue risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Positive short-term effect mitigates net risk, yielding low score.
